title: Gateway route tagging plan (telemetry join keys) — cache + inference metrics
content:
Context / why
- Cache telemetry sprint requires slicing + joining runtime cache metrics with tenant/route/model context (model version consistency is the recurring pain point).
- Today we have a mix of tags across systems:
  - Gateway request logs include route path templates + some model name, but not stable IDs everywhere.
  - Runtime metrics historically used model string labels (often inconsistent) and no canonical route identifier.
  - Console analytics tables use a route_id, but the runtime doesn’t always see it.
- Goal: define + implement a consistent set of low-cardinality, join-friendly identifiers that can be propagated from gateway -> runtime -> metrics/traces/logs, without blowing up cardinality and without breaking existing dashboards.

Non-goals
- Not attempting to create customer-facing “semantic route naming” UX in this sprint.
- Not logging prompts or any prompt-derived identifiers (privacy). No per-request unique IDs in metrics.

Requirements (from Telemetry + SRE)
- Join keys must be consistent across:
  - gateway access logs
  - runtime metrics (cache hit/miss + eviction pressure + wasted prefill)
  - traces (span attributes) for correlation
  - analytics aggregates (batch job for recommendations)
- Must support breakdowns by:
  - model + model_version
  - route (customer-configured route in Redwood control plane)
  - deployment mode: hosted / dedicated / private
  - region
- Cardinality constraints:
  - Avoid raw path (e.g., /v1/chat/completions?user_id=...) in labels.
  - Avoid per-tenant labels on high-volume metrics unless allowlisted / bucketed.
  - Prefer stable IDs over free-form strings; any string labels must be from an allowlist.

Plan of record: canonical tag set
We will standardize on the following canonical identifiers.

A) Tenant / workspace identity
- tenant_id: stable Redwood tenant/workspace UUID (string). Source: auth context after API key/JWT validation.
  - Metrics: NOT always emitted as label (see cardinality rules below). When emitted, it must be allowlisted sampling-only.
  - Traces/logs: safe to include.
- tenant_tier: enum string (free | paid | enterprise). Source: control plane. Low cardinality; OK in metrics.

B) Route identity (control-plane route)
- route_id: stable UUID from control plane. This is the primary join key.
  - Example: "rt_01HR8D3R3R2K3C9XJ0ZJ2W6GQ9" (format TBD; must be stable and opaque)
- route_name: short, sanitized string (optional). Only emitted if it passes allowlist + regex.
  - Intended for UI convenience in traces/logs. Avoid metrics by default.
- route_type: enum (chat_completions | completions | embeddings | rerank | other). Low cardinality.

C) Model identity
- model_id: Redwood catalog ID (or customer-provided model slot ID for Dedicated/Private). Stable, opaque.
- model_version_id: stable version identifier. MUST be the same across:
  - gateway request context
  - runtime model loader
  - metrics/traces
  Notes:
  - For hosted curated models, model_version_id comes from the model registry.
  - For dedicated/private, model_version_id should map to the deployed artifact digest/sha + control-plane version record.
- model_family: optional enum-ish label (llama | mistral | qwen | gemma | other). Used for dashboard grouping; must be allowlisted.

D) Deployment / locality
- deployment_mode: enum (hosted | dedicated | private).
- region: short region code (us-east-1 | us-west-2 | eu-west-1 | ...). Must match existing infra standards.
- cluster_id: OPTIONAL. Only for internal debugging; should be trace/log only (high cardinality risk).

E) Request shape bucketing (for cache telemetry)
- prompt_len_bucket: enum bucket (e.g., 0-256, 256-1k, 1k-4k, 4k-8k, 8k+).
- prefill_tokens_bucket / total_tokens_bucket: histogram-style bucket labels controlled by runtime/standards.
- stream: boolean string ("true"/"false") (optional; careful: adds 2x series).

Cardinality policy (practical rules)
1) Metrics MUST always include:
   - model_id
   - model_version_id
   - route_id
   - deployment_mode
   - region
   - plus whatever bucket labels the metric definition requires (prompt_len_bucket, etc.)
2) Metrics MUST NOT include by default:
   - tenant_id (except allowlisted tenants / sampled debug mode)
   - route_name
   - raw http path
   - api_key_id or user_id
3) Traces MAY include:
   - tenant_id
   - route_name (sanitized)
   - request_id
4) Logs MAY include:
   - tenant_id
   - route_id
   - model_version_id
   - but must avoid raw prompts and any customer PII.

Where tags live (implementation)
- Gateway (API edge)
  - Constructs a RequestContext struct after auth + routing decision.
  - Adds the canonical identifiers to:
    - outgoing request headers (to runtime)
    - trace context (span attributes)
    - access log fields
- Runtime (serving)
  - Reads request headers into its own RequestContext.
  - Emits metrics with tag allowlist enforcement (runtime-side) + ingestion-side cardinality guards.

Header propagation (gateway -> runtime)
Proposed headers (names subject to final review; keep them short):
- x-rw-route-id: <route_id>
- x-rw-model-id: <model_id>
- x-rw-model-version-id: <model_version_id>
- x-rw-deployment-mode: hosted|dedicated|private
- x-rw-region: <region>
- x-rw-tenant-id: <tenant_id> (trace/log only by default; runtime can read but metrics should drop unless debug flag)

Notes:
- If we already have a request metadata header mechanism, prefer adding these fields to that envelope instead of creating many headers.
- Private/VPC deployments: if customers run the gateway, headers must be supported in the on-prem package too.

Backwards compatibility / migration strategy
Current state (rough):
- Some dashboards slice by model="Llama-3.1-70B" or route="/v1/chat/completions".
- Some metrics use model_name/model_version as strings; some have missing route.

Migration approach: dual-write + alias period
Phase 0 (now): Define mapping + publish in standards (Nadia owns schema).
Phase 1 (canary):
- Gateway emits new canonical context fields.
- Runtime metrics start emitting NEW labels for a limited set of metrics (cache only) behind a feature flag.
- Observability pack adds panels using the new labels, but keeps old panels intact.
Phase 2 (prod rollout):
- Enable gateway propagation globally.
- Enable runtime emission globally with sampling + ingestion guards.
- Backfill / update dashboard defaults to prefer route_id/model_version_id.
Phase 3 (deprecation):
- Mark old labels/metric names as deprecated.
- Remove old panels/alerts after 2 release cycles.

Important: avoid “label rename breaks queries”
- We should avoid changing label keys in-place on existing metric names. Prefer either:
  - new metric names (if renaming is necessary), or
  - temporarily emitting both old and new labels (only if series impact is acceptable), or
  - ingestion-side relabeling for compatibility (Caleb to advise).

Joinability and consistency checks
We need a sanity matrix and automated checks:
- For each request sample in canary:
  - gateway log route_id/model_version_id == runtime trace route_id/model_version_id
  - runtime metric tags (aggregated) include route_id/model_version_id combos that exist in gateway logs
- Add a daily job/query (Mei / analytics) to check:
  - % of traffic missing route_id
  - % missing model_version_id
  - top mismatched model_version_id between gateway and runtime
- SRE dashboard: “Tag coverage” panel.

Edge cases / gotchas
1) Streaming retries
- If gateway retries a stream and creates a new upstream request, ensure route_id/model_version_id remain identical.
- Runtime must avoid double counting (handled in separate runtime PR, but tags must not cause duplicate series).

2) Batched prefill / continuous batching
- A runtime batch can contain multiple route_id/model_version_id combinations.
- Metrics must attribute per-request, not per-batch, OR explicitly bucket “mixed batches” (strong preference: per-request attribution).

3) Model fallback / smart routing
- If gateway routes to a fallback model_version_id due to capacity:
  - route_id should remain the same (customer asked for route X)
  - model_version_id should reflect what actually ran
  - OPTIONAL: requested_model_id/requested_model_version_id (trace only; do NOT put in metrics initially)

4) Private deployments / customer-managed gateways
- If the customer is running a private gateway build, we must ensure:
  - route_id generation/assignment is still consistent with control-plane
  - model_version_id corresponds to the deployed artifact in that environment
  - region semantics might be different (still require a stable region label; can be "onprem" or customer region code).

5) Multi-tenant Dedicated clusters
- route_id is still per-tenant, but a dedicated cluster may host multiple “routes” with same underlying model.
- Keep route_id as the join key; do not use raw path.

Open questions
- route_id format: do we want UUIDv4, snowflake, or existing "rt_" IDs? Requirement is “opaque and stable”.
- Should we emit tenant_id in metrics for Dedicated only (lower tenant count) to help debugging? SRE leaning “no by default”.
- Do we need route_group_id (e.g., canonical route across versions) for long-lived dashboards?
- model_family label: maintain allowlist in control plane or in telemetry ingestion?

Implementation tasks (owner / notes)
- Gateway: populate RequestContext and propagate headers (Amara, Ethan)
  - Add integration test: request -> upstream sees x-rw-* headers.
  - Ensure headers are stripped at egress (never to customer callbacks/webhooks).
- Control plane / config: ensure route_id + model_version_id always available at routing decision time (Ethan)
- Runtime: read new headers into metric tag context (Omar / Samir)
  - Enforce metric label allowlist (drop tenant_id, route_name).
- Ingestion: cardinality guard updates (Caleb)
  - Drop/aggregate any unexpected label keys.
- Dashboards: update queries to use route_id/model_version_id (Allison)

Rollout + gating
- Stage: validate tag coverage > 99% and no metric series explosion beyond budget.
- Canary: 5% traffic in us-east-1 hosted; compare:
  - p95/p99 latency
  - metric ingest volume (series + samples/sec)
  - cache hit-rate deltas should be explainable (not an artifact of tagging).
- Prod: expand region by region; disable quickly by feature flag.

Notes to self / misc
- Keep a short “tag dictionary” in the runtime repo README once merged (link from PR-18426/18434).
- Make sure route_id and model_version_id are present in the recommendation batch job outputs so CS can cross-reference easily.
- If we find model_version_id isn’t stable for private/on-prem, we may need a separate "artifact_digest" field (trace only) and map it upstream in analytics.
